title: Dry-run environment sweep for Private installs: quotas, IAM, DNS, GPU capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a non-destructive 'dry-run sweep' tool and Terraform data modules that validate a target cloud environment before a Redwood Private (VPC) installation. The sweep must check regional quotas (vCPU, GPUs, IPs), required IAM roles/policies, DNS delegation/resolution for private zones, and GPU SKU compatibility + node pool capacity. The scope covers AWS and GCP initial rollouts; design should be extensible to Azure. This ticket produces: a reusable Terraform data module set, a CLI command (redwoodctl precheck:sweep), CI validation jobs, and remediation hints surfaced to operators.
tasks: Design Terraform data modules to query quotas and available SKUs for AWS & GCP (data.aws_servicequotas, GCP serviceusage/compute quotas equivalents)
Create a Terraform 'check' module that can be run in read-only mode to synthesize a pass/fail JSON report (no resource creation)
Implement redwoodctl subcommand 'precheck sweep' that calls the Terraform module and cloud SDK fallbacks for checks that Terraform cannot query reliably
Add explicit IAM role/policy matrix checks: verify service account permissions, KMS access, and cross-account role assumptions used by Private control plane
DNS checks: verify private zone exists/has delegation to VPC (AWS Route53) or private DNS peering (GCP Cloud DNS), and that resolver IPs are reachable from the expected subnets
GPU capacity checks: list available instance/GPU SKUs in region, check quota vs requested node pool size; surface driver compatibility notes and suggested instance types
Create heuristics for ephemeral 'capacity reservation' simulation: attempt to create provider quota request objects (dry) or evaluate current reservations across tenant accounts
Integrate check reporting with Console: upload JSON report to customer Console under 'Private Deploy Health' and link to runbook
Write unit and integration tests for Terraform modules and the CLI path using recorded cloud responses (VCR/mock fixtures)
Author operator remediation hints and automated next-step commands for common failures (quota increase request snippets, IAM policy diffs)
Add CI gates: run sweep on PRs that touch private deploy modules and fail PR if critical prechecks regress
acceptance_criteria: redwoodctl precheck sweep runs against a customer account (AWS/GCP) and returns exit codes: 0=ok, 1=warnings, 2=blocking-failure
Output is a machine-readable JSON report with per-check id, status (pass/warn/fail), actionable message, and remediation link
Terraform data modules are published to the private registry and consumed by the installer module without creating resources

Automated remediation hints exist for top 8 failure modes (quota, IAM missing role, DNS delegation, GPU SKU unavailable, insufficient VPC IPs, missing KMS permissions, firewall rules, missing service APIs)
E2E test simulates an account with a quota shortfall and demonstrates the report highlights the missing quota and includes suggested quota increase payload
Documentation updated (installer runbook + Quickstart doc) with examples and sample outputs
Security review completed and security_review_required set to true with reviewer sign-off recorded in comments
notes: Trade-offs: some quota queries are eventually-consistent (esp. GCP); tool will prefer direct provider APIs over Terraform when consistency matters. This is more brittle but provides timelier answers.
Decision: start with AWS and GCP only for this sprint; collect telemetry on common failure modes before adding Azure. API differences will be abstracted behind a small provider adapter interface.
We intentionally avoid creating ephemeral heavy resources (no instance launches). Where necessary, we simulate via provider quota APIs or use lightweight reads to infer capacity.
We will reuse parts of the existing 'terraform preinstall assertion' work but must not duplicate checks; focus on cloud-provider-specific queries and actionable remediation text.
Risk: querying quotas at scale may hit rate limits for large customers. Implement exponential backoff and aggregated batching per-region.
Performance goal: full sweep should complete in <90s for a typical region+account pair; anything slower should run asynchronously with progress telemetry
